title: Forward Deployed Software Engineer, Internship - UK Government
sections: Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

Forward Deployed Engineering is a radical commitment to the outcome. This is Palantir’s operating ethos. We pioneered this unique position, embedding engineers directly with our customers to tackle their most pressing challenges head-on. As an FDE, you’ll be at the intersection of world-changing problems and impactful technology, shaping solutions where they matter most.
From hospital beds to factory floors, Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) embed themselves in the customer’s reality until the problem is theirs. This requires walking many miles in a customer’s shoes, building past the perimeter of what the product currently offers, and deviating from every pre-existing formula to solve the problem. Whether that problem is “How do we predict and mitigate wildfire risks across a power grid?” or “How can we analyze and adapt a global supply chain to deliver critical parts on time?”, you’ll use your technical expertise, creativity, and problem-solving skills to drive real-world impact.

To solve mission-critical problems by deploying software and AI into the high stakes operations of the world’s leading institutions. This requires a ruthless commitment to truth-seeking and prioritizing real outcomes.
The work is difficult. The stakes are real. You will work in small, high-trust teams and own projects end-to-end, from the first conversation with a customer, to shipping the product that changes how they operate. You will embed with the customer, the chaos, and the consequences, and will be entrusted with real ownership to:
Collaborate with engineers to make architecture and design decisions
Wrestle with data at a scale that breaks assumptions and demands invention
Build custom applications, LLM workflows, and production solutions engineered for a specific customer's reality
Own relationships with stakeholders from the users in the weeds to the executives making the calls
As an Intern, you will be entrusted with responsibility on day 1 and expected to learn quickly. You will not be handed a low-risk or unimportant project. You will not be shielded from the customer, the chaos, or the consequences. FDEs are entrusted with real ownership, operating with real autonomy, and held to a real standard, no matter their tenure.

In an effort to build more transparency into our recruitment process, we’d like to share our offer deadline expectations. By applying to this position, you commit to confirming your decision within two weeks of receiving your written offer.

We want every Palantirian to achieve their best outcomes, that’s why we celebrate individuals’ strengths, skills, and interests, from your first interview to your longterm growth, rather than rely on traditional career ladders. Paying attention to the needs of our community enables us to optimize our opportunities to grow and helps ensure many pathways to success at Palantir. Promoting health and well-being across all areas of Palantirians’ lives is just one of the ways we’re investing in our community. Learn more at Life at Palantir and note that our offerings may vary by region.
In keeping consistent with Palantir’s values and culture, we believe employees are “better together” and in-person work affords the opportunity for more creative outcomes. Therefore, we encourage employees to work from our offices to foster connectivity and innovation. Many teams do offer hybrid options (WFH a day or two a week), allowing our employees to strike the right trade-off for their personal productivity. Based on business need, there are a few roles that allow for “Remote” work on an exceptional basis. If you are applying for one of these roles, you must work from the city and or country in which you are employed. If the posting is specified as Onsite, you are required to work from an office.
If you want to empower the world's most important institutions, you belong here. Palantir values excellence regardless of background. We are committed to making the application and hiring process accessible to everyone and will provide a reasonable accommodation for those living with a disability. If you need an accommodation for the application or hiring process, please reach out and let us know how we can help.
Please note that you will never be asked to submit a payment or share financial information to participate in our interview process. If you suspect that you've been contacted by a scammer, we recommend you cease all communication with the individual and consider reporting them to the relevant authorities, such as the US FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3).

The drive to solve your customer’s problem. This can translate to:
Going where you’re needed most — Embed where and when it matters. Expect 25–50% travel, depending on team and location.
Agency — You learn continuously, make decisions with incomplete information, and don't wait to be told what to do next.
Embracing the ambiguity — You operate effectively in teams that mix technical and non-technical people, in environments where the objectives shift, the users push back, and the solution demands iteration.
Intrinsic motivations — You solve hard technical problems (data structures, storage systems, cloud infrastructure, front-end frameworks) not because you were assigned to, but because that's what it takes to achieve your outcomes.
Ruthless goal orientation — You do not operate within a product’s existing boundaries and limitations. You push past them, rewrite them, or discard them entirely.

title: Senior AI Evals Engineer
sections: The Senior AI Evals Test Engineer is a hands-on technical role responsible for defining, developing, and executing robust evaluation frameworks and test strategies for AI agents built using the Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) or similar sort of agentic frameworks. This role bridges AI development and reliable deployment — ensuring our agents are safe, ethical, effective, and meet high-quality performance standards. A significant focus of the role is on Responsible AI and Safety Evals, including adversarial testing, red-teaming, bias detection, and toxicity measurement. The engineer will design scalable evaluation pipelines, build synthetic test environments, and work closely with AI/ML Engineers, Researchers, and policy teams to ensure agents are production-ready and compliant with regulatory and ethical standards. The role is 70% Automation and 30% Manual Testing, and sits within the Applied AI: Test Engineering team as a key technical authority.

Design and build agent evaluation frameworks — create end-to-end infrastructure for evaluating LLM-based agents across correctness, latency, cost, safety, and task completion rate
Build synthetic testing environments and simulation strategies to stress-test AI agents under diverse real-world conditions, with specific focus on agents built on Google ADK and related Google AI/ML services (e.g., Vertex AI, Gemini models)
Build golden datasets and test harnesses — curate domain-specific evaluation sets for Rubrik's product verticals (data security, SaaS protection, cyber recovery, compliance)
Establish eval-as-a-service — build and enhance centralized evaluation platform that any IT team members can self-serve to test their agents against standardized and custom benchmarks
Automate regression and drift detection — implement CI/CD-integrated eval pipelines that catch regressions on every model or prompt change before production deployment
Define eval taxonomies and rubrics — establish structured scoring criteria for agentic workflows (tool use accuracy, multi-step reasoning, hallucination rate, policy adherence, error recovery)
Instrument production observability — build real-time monitoring for agent quality in production: success rates, user corrections, fallback triggers, escalation patterns
Benchmark and select models — run structured model comparisons (cost, quality, latency trade-offs) to inform model selection decisions across agent use cases
Analyze and interpret evaluation results, providing clear, actionable quality and safety reports to stakeholders and development teams, with specific focus on risk metrics, trend analysis, and mitigation recommendations
Define comprehensive end-to-end QA strategies — functional, integration, regression, and user acceptance testing (UAT) — tailored for conversational and goal-oriented AI agents with tool-use, memory, and multi-turn reasoning capabilities
Develop and maintain detailed test artifacts (test plans, test cases, test scenarios, automated test suites) covering agent features, tool invocation, memory persistence, and reasoning accuracy across evolving model versions
Identify, document, prioritize, and track defects, performance regressions, and alignment failures using Jira, collaborating closely with Applied AI Engineers to analyze root causes and validate fixes
Evaluate new technologies and patterns (e.g., new tools for Agent Evals), run proofs-of-concept, and influence the platform roadmap
Partner with policy and legal teams to ensure agent evaluations systematically cover regulatory compliance, fairness objectives, and emerging AI governance requirements
Provide technical leadership to engineers, including solutioning, design reviews, code reviews, pair programming, and mentoring of junior and contract engineers
Collaborate cross-functionally — work closely with ML engineers, product teams, platform engineers, and security to embed eval-driven quality gates into the agent development lifecycle

We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Lead major-version upgrades, snapshot and disaster recovery strategy, and multi-cluster architectures

Index and mapping design, and why those choices drive cluster performance
Lifecycle and retention across data tiers, including the cost and latency implications of each
Snapshot, restore and disaster recovery designed and executed, not just configured
Major-version upgrades in production — the sequencing, the breaking changes, the rollback position

Cluster stability and performance troubleshooting — heap and garbage collection, circuit breakers, thread pool rejections, shard allocation, expensive queries

At Palantir, the Forward Deployed Software Engineer (FDSE) role isn’t just a job title: it’s the blueprint. We pioneered this unique position, embedding talented engineers directly with our customers to tackle their most pressing challenges head-on. As an FDSE, you’ll be at the intersection of world-changing problems and impactful technology, shaping solutions where they matter most.
FDSEs work side by side with our customers, rapidly understanding their toughest issues; architecting and building solutions that leverage business-critical data and the latest advancements in AI to solve them. title: Senior Staff Machine Learning Engineer, Ads Ranking
sections:
Reddit is a community of communities. It’s built on shared interests, passion, and trust, and is home to the most open and authentic conversations on the internet. Every day, Reddit users submit, vote, and comment on the topics they care most about. With 100,000+ active communities and approximately 130 million daily active unique visitors, Reddit is one of the internet’s largest sources of information. For more information, visit www.redditinc.com.
We are seeking a Senior Staff Machine Learning Engineer to lead the technical direction of Reddit’s Core Ads Ranking and mid-funnel modeling systems. Operating as a hands-on technical leader, you will advance user representation, graph learning, and sequence modeling across ads verticals—building foundational architectures that power downstream teams including Retrieval, Shopping, Click Prediction, Video View-Through Prediction, Conversion Prediction, and App Ads Modeling.
In addition to driving core ranking breakthroughs, you will elevate how ML engineering is executed across the org—leveraging modern AI-assisted development workflows (such as Claude, Cursor, and comparable tools) to accelerate experimentation, deepen error analysis, and raise the bar for modeling rigor and velocity.
Why Join Us? This role offers a high-leverage technical platform to shape and scale Reddit’s foundational ads modeling and deep user-understanding roadmap. If you are passionate about solving complex ranking, calibration, and sequence modeling problems at scale—while utilizing cutting-edge AI workflows to multiply your team's modeling impact—we’d love to talk to you.

Set Foundational Modeling Vision: Define and execute the technical roadmap for Core Ads Ranking, user representation, graph learning, and sequence modeling across mid-funnel objectives (clicks, video views, and conversions), balancing long-term foundational bets with measurable production gains.
Advance Core Ranking & Distillation: Lead high-impact initiatives in foundational model architectures, knowledge distillation, model calibration, and feature/embedding development to maximize model quality, reliability, and serving efficiency.
Multiply Impact Across Verticals: Partner closely with downstream vertical teams (Retrieval, Shopping, App Ads, Video, and Conversion modeling), data science, product, and ML infrastructure to align on shared signals, architectures, and business outcomes.
Accelerate the Modeling Loop with AI Tooling: Utilize AI-assisted development systems (Claude, Cursor, etc.) to investigate model behavior, automate hypothesis testing and error analysis, and build reliable, reproducible loops for architecture comparison, hyperparameter optimization, and experiment readouts.
Design Rigorous Evaluation Harnesses: Build robust evaluation frameworks that measure both ranking/calibration outcomes and workflow quality, ensuring correctness, reproducibility, and strict latency/cost adherence.
Provide Senior Staff Technical Leadership: Mentor engineers across the ads organization, guide technical design reviews, and elevate engineering standards for modeling rigor and modern ML workflows.

9+ years of experience in machine learning engineering, applied ML, or a related field, with a track record of substantial production impact at scale.
Senior Staff-level technical leadership: Proven ability to set technical direction, drive alignment across multiple teams, and solve ambiguous, high-stakes modeling problems without direct management authority.
Deep Ranking & Foundational ML Expertise: Strong fundamentals in large-scale recommendation/ads ranking systems, sequence modeling, graph learning, user/content understanding, model calibration, and knowledge distillation.
End-to-End Modeling Fluency: Hands-on expertise in Python and modern ML frameworks (PyTorch or TensorFlow), covering data/label analysis, architecture design, distributed training, and production deployment.
Modern AI-Assisted Engineering Mindset: Practical experience leveraging AI coding or agentic development tools to accelerate hypothesis generation, automate deep error analysis, and produce measurably better ML outcomes.
Collaborative, Low-Ego Communicator: Clear, concise communication skills with the ability to influence both deep technical specialists and cross-functional product partners.

sections: Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies, from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups, use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

Stripe's Money Management products (Financial Accounts, Treasury, Global Payouts, Issuing, and Capital) let businesses and platforms hold, move, spend, and earn on their money using the same infrastructure they already use for payments. APAC Money as a Service (MaaS) is a newly formed team, based in Singapore, responsible for bringing this product suite to Asia-Pacific markets, enabling global businesses and platforms to use these capabilities directly or offer them to their APAC users, and building the local rails, compliance, and partner integrations that make it all work.
None of this works without financial partners: the banks, card networks, and licensed institutions whose systems our products run on in each market. Technical Operations in APAC MaaS owns the day-to-day health of those partner integrations, existing and new, and the working technical relationship with the partners behind them. We sit between product and platform engineering, Stripe's partnerships and compliance teams, and our partners' technical teams, which gives us an unusually complete view of how money moves in the region: the code and the real-world mechanics behind it.

This role sits where Stripe's engineering meets the financial institutions we build on, and it is broader than most technical operations seats. You'll own the health of the partner integrations that power APAC MaaS, and you'll be the technical face of Stripe to the banks, networks, and institutions behind them. One week that means working through a partner specification and reconciling settlement files; the next, shipping tooling or running an operational review with a partner's engineering team. Because every APAC launch depends on partner readiness, you'll have direct line of sight into what the team ships and a real say in how. It's a role that builds technical depth and partner judgment at the same time, in a region where we're still writing the playbook.

Own the operational health of APAC MaaS's financial partner integrations across accounts, payouts, and card issuing: monitor them, catch problems early, and drive issues to root cause and durable fixes.
Act as the primary technical point of contact for our partners in the region. Run recurring operational reviews, manage escalations end to end, align on product usage and specifications, and keep both Stripe and the partner on track against their commitments.
Lead partner-facing technical change: onboarding and certifying new integrations, specification changes, migrations and cutovers, and incident reviews, coordinating Stripe engineering, partnerships, compliance, and the partner's teams.
Investigate and resolve issues across the stack. Read and write code, query data, work through logs and partner reports and files, and make scoped changes in Stripe's codebase when that is the right fix.
Build reconciliation and anomaly detection so that money moving through our partner integrations is correct, traceable, and accounted for, in collaboration with engineering, accounting, and partnerships.
Remove manual work through code, tooling, or changes to how we operate with partners.
Become the team's domain expert on how money actually moves in each APAC market: rails, cutoffs, settlement cycles, file formats, return codes, and partner-specific behavior. Document it and make it usable by the rest of the team.
Bring partner realities into product and engineering decisions, and define what "partner-ready" means for each market launch.

You're equally at home in a partner's steering call and in a debugger, and you enjoy moving between the two. You are precise: you read the specification to the end, you notice when a reconciliation is off by one record, and you follow up until the loose end is closed. You build trust with external counterparts by being prepared, direct, and reliable, and you can hold a partner (or Stripe) to a commitment while keeping the relationship strong.

We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

title: Engineering Manager - Grafana Infrastructure (Remote, Ireland)
sections:
Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.
We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.
You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.
This is a remote position and we're considering candidates in the UK, Spain or Ireland.

Grafana Cloud moves millions of metrics, log lines, and traces per second from our customers' environments into a highly available, low-latency stack that processes and stores this data, and serves it to dashboards and alerting tools. We aim to grow this to hundreds of millions per second, and it's critical that as we grow, we improve our performance, increase our reliability, and do it efficiently and securely.
The Foundations department owns the Internal Engineering Platform (IEP): the Kubernetes clusters, cloud service provider resources (CSP), hardware, identity, delivery, and observability systems that Grafana Labs's application engineers use to build, deploy, and run their workloads.

We're hiring an engineering manager for the Foundations Infrastructure group, which owns the cloud infrastructure Grafana Cloud runs on. The group provisions and operates Kubernetes clusters and CSP resources across GCP, AWS, and Azure; enforces identity, access, and security controls across those environments; and runs the observability and cost-visibility systems that keep the infrastructure measurable and accountable.
You'll lead one of the squads of platform engineers that comprise the group.
We're platform engineers, and our application teams are our users. Our job is to give them leverage: self-service building blocks that take care of the hard parts of infrastructure, so they can focus on what they're building. We treat the platform as a product and value the experience of the people who use it. When a change is well communicated and understood, teams welcome it, and it lands as an improvement that makes the right way the easy way. You'll lead a squad that makes that happen.

Foundations is a global team that works asynchronously. The people who own a component or problem make the decisions about it, once stakeholders have had a chance to weigh in. Application teams build and run their own services; we give them a self-service platform to do it on.
Every engineer is on-call for the components their squad provides. We plan on-call, tactical work, and time off into every quarter, so roadmap work is roughly half of an engineer's time rather than all of it.

Hire, manage, and develop a squad of platform engineers, with regular feedback and career conversations that support each person's growth.
Own your squad's roadmap and quarterly objectives: help decide what the squad works on, what it defers, and why, across a broad remit where demand always exceeds capacity.
Take platform changes from design to fleet-wide adoption: staged rollouts, migration paths, and clear communication, so changes land well for the teams who depend on them.
Partner with the other Infrastructure squads on work that spans them, and with the teams across Foundations and the rest of Engineering whose work depends on yours.
Help shape how the group works as a whole, including planning, on-call, and the ownership model between squads.
Own the squad's intake. Requests, reviews, and support from application teams arrive continuously; keep them triaged and visible so that planned work still moves.
Keep on-call healthy: ensure a sustainable load and support incident response.
Work across team boundaries, contributing beyond your squad's scope where Foundations needs it.
We invest heavily in developer productivity. You can use modern AI coding assistants as part of your daily workflow (your choice of tools, within security guidelines), backed by a company-funded usage budget so you can iterate quickly without unnecessary friction.
We encourage pragmatic AI-assisted development: faster prototyping, test generation, refactors, documentation, and incident follow-ups, always paired with strong code review and quality standards.
What Makes You a Great Fit

Experience managing engineers, ideally a team that builds and operates production CSP infrastructure, security, networking and/or storage
Hands-on depth in at least one area of platform engineering, such as cloud infrastructure and Kubernetes, infrastructure security and access, or observability. You can challenge a design in your area on its merits, and the engineers on your team will expect you to.
Fluency with infrastructure as code and with running Kubernetes in production.
A track record of landing internal engineering/developer platform changes at scale. You've driven a migration or a rollout across many teams or many clusters, and you know what makes one stall.
The ability to explain platform engineering to very different audiences (platform engineers, application teams, product management and business leadership) and to make the case for what the squad should and shouldn't take on.
Be comfortable collaborating across time zones and cultures in a fully remote environment, using clear, written communication to build trust and psychological safety.
You're a motivated self-starter with a strong bias toward action and ownership, able to navigate ambiguity in a complex problem space.
Comfort with AI-assisted tooling. We embrace AI and agentic development, so we expect you to be curious and comfortable using AI-powered tools, and ideally to have practical experience folding them into a team's workflow.

Experience across more than one of the group's areas: cloud infrastructure, infrastructure security, and observability
Hands-on depth in cloud infrastructure security: cloud IAM, Kubernetes security, secrets, and workload identity on at least one major cloud provider. You can challenge a threat model or an access design on its merits, and the engineers on your team will expect you to.
Building self-service infrastructure for application teams
Running observability for a production platform at scale
Operating across more than one of GCP, AWS, and Azure
You've worked in or on open source, or other community-based projects. At Grafana Labs, "OSS is in our DNA"
